body:
Closing as already covered.

When I opened this issue, the `conformance/` directory existed but there was no documented cross-language harness — that gap is now closed:

- `conformance/cross_language_check.py` runs Python, Rust, and TypeScript implementations against the same shared fixtures and asserts byte-exact agreement on canonical bytes (added in `0.8.2`, runners completed in `0.8.3`, Rust/TS runners verified in CI in `0.8.4`).
- `conformance/CROSS_LANGUAGE.md` documents the contract, the fixture format, and how to add a 4th implementation (added in `0.8.2`).
- The CI workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the cross-language job on every push, building the Rust helper and running all three implementations together (added in `0.8.4`).

The README's cross-language section now points to the harness as the executable evidence backing the "cross-validation confirms" claim.

The original acceptance criteria for this issue (verify Python/Rust/TS commands, explain shared-vector contract, document one-language-failure semantics) are all met by `conformance/CROSS_LANGUAGE.md`.

Thanks to @soyeladice-svg for picking it up and being honest about releasing the assignment when the scope turned out larger than expected — that feedback prompted me to look at whether the issue was even still needed, and it isn't.

Closing as completed by the `0.8.2`–`0.8.4` audit pass.
